entities.summary:
The Siege of Lisbon, which took place from 1147-10-25 to 1147-11-01, was a pivotal event in the history of Portugal. This 1147 siege, involving the city of al-Lixbûnâ, was a significant turning point in the Christian Reconquista of the Iberian Peninsula, marking a crucial moment in the expansion of Christian control and the eventual Christianization of Portugal. The siege was a key moment in the broader struggle between Christian and Muslim forces in the region, with the city changing hands several times before finally falling to Christian forces. This event had lasting consequences for the region, shaping the course of medieval history in the Iberian Peninsula and beyond.

The siege was a complex and multifaceted event, involving a range of key figures and forces. The city of Lisbon, strategically located on the Tagus River, was a crucial prize in the struggle for control of the region. The siege was marked by a series of intense battles and negotiations, ultimately resulting in the city's capture by Christian forces. This event had significant implications for the region, leading to a period of Christian domination and the eventual establishment of the Kingdom of Portugal.

The legacy of the Siege of Lisbon can be seen in the lasting impact it had on the region. The event marked a significant turning point in the Christian Reconquista, paving the way for the eventual Christianization of the Iberian Peninsula. This had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of medieval history and beyond. The siege also had a lasting impact on the city of Lisbon, which became a major center of Christian power and influence in the region.
